title.zh: 卷458 列傳二百四十五 徐延旭 唐炯 何璟 张兆栋
title.en: Volume 458 Biographies 245: Xu Yanxu, Tang Jiong, He Jing, Zhang Zhaodong
title.raw: 卷458 列傳二百四十五 徐延旭 唐炯 何璟 张兆栋

sentences.zh: 徐延旭，字曉山，山東臨清人。

translations.literal: Xu Yanxu, style name Xiaoshan, was a native of Linqing in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanxu, whose style was Xiaoshan, came from Linqing in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年進士，出知廣西容縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of the Xianfeng reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Rong County in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the tenth year of Xianfeng and was sent out to serve as magistrate of Rong County in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 師克潯州，與有功，累晉知府。

translations.literal: When the army captured Xunzhou he had merit in the affair and was repeatedly promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself when the army took Xunzhou and was promoted step by step to prefect.

sentences.zh: 同治九年，除知梧州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Tongzhi reign he was appointed magistrate of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tongzhi he was appointed magistrate of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，遷安襄荊鄖道。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Guangxu reign he was transferred to the An-Xiang-Jing-Min circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he was transferred to the An-Xiang-Jing-Min circuit intendant post.

sentences.zh: 八年，晉廣西布政使，命督辦海防，得專奏事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Guangxi provincial treasurer and ordered to supervise coastal defense, with authority to memorialize the throne on his own.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Guangxi provincial treasurer, charged with supervising coastal defense and granted the right to submit memorials directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時法人謀佔全越，巡撫張之洞、侍讀張佩綸先後疏薦堪軍事。

translations.literal: At that time the French were plotting to seize all of Annam; the governor Zhang Zhidong and the Hanlin reader Zhang Peilun successively memorialized recommending him as capable in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The French were then scheming to occupy all of Vietnam, and both Governor Zhang Zhidong and Hanlin reader Zhang Peilun memorialized the throne in turn, commending Xu as fit for military command.

sentences.zh: 會南定陷，朝命出鎮南關，與提督黃桂蘭、道員趙沃籌防，未行，越官劉永福戰勝懷德府紙橋，狀其績以上。

translations.literal: When Nam Dinh fell the court ordered him out to garrison Zhennan Pass, to plan defense together with the provincial military commander Huang Guilan and the circuit intendant Zhao Wo; before he set out, the Annamese officer Liu Yongfu won a battle at Paper Bridge in Huai De prefecture and reported his achievements upward.
translations.idiomatic: When Nam Dinh fell, the court ordered him to take command at Zhennan Pass and plan the defense with Provincial Military Commander Huang Guilan and Circuit Intendant Zhao Wo. Before he marched, the Vietnamese officer Liu Yongfu won a victory at Paper Bridge in Huai De prefecture and submitted a report of his exploits.

sentences.zh: 九年，出關，至北寧而還，頓龍州，被命為巡撫，敕趣永福規河內。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out through the pass, reached Bac Ninh and returned, halted at Longzhou, was appointed governor, and was ordered to urge Yongfu to scheme against Hanoi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he crossed the border, advanced as far as Bac Ninh, then withdrew and encamped at Longzhou. He was appointed governor and instructed to press Yongfu to move against Hanoi.

sentences.zh: 延旭上部署防守狀，略云：「固廣西邊疆，必守北寧；

translations.literal: Yanxu submitted a memorial on deployment for defense, stating in summary: "To secure Guangxi's frontier one must hold Bac Ninh;
translations.idiomatic: Yanxu submitted a memorial outlining his defensive dispositions, which in essence read: "To secure the Guangxi frontier, Bac Ninh must be held;

sentences.zh: 固雲南邊疆，必守山西。

translations.literal: to secure Yunnan's frontier one must hold Son Tay.
translations.idiomatic: to secure the Yunnan frontier, Son Tay must be held.

sentences.zh: 左軍前鋒分駐北寧、湧球，去城止十二里。

translations.literal: The vanguard of the left army was divided between garrisons at Bac Ninh and Yungqiu, only twelve li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: The left army's vanguard was split between Bac Ninh and Yungqiu, a mere twelve li from the city.

sentences.zh: 一旦有事，援之則無辭於法，聽之則有慚於越。

translations.literal: If trouble arose at once, to rescue them would give the French a pretext, while to stand by would bring shame before Annam.
translations.idiomatic: If fighting broke out, reinforcing them would give France a grievance, while leaving them to their fate would be a disgrace before Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 不如徙軍入城，城固我儲糧屯戍所也。

translations.literal: It would be better to move the troops into the city, for the city was after all our depot for stored grain and garrison stores.
translations.idiomatic: Better to move the troops into the city, which was in any case our depot for grain stores and garrison supplies.

sentences.zh: 並簡銳扼浪泊湖北岸，為山西聲援；

translations.literal: He also selected crack troops to hold the north bank of Lang Bo Lake as a supporting force for Son Tay;
translations.idiomatic: He also picked elite troops to hold the north bank of Lang Bo Lake as a flank for Son Tay;

sentences.zh: 別募勇百人扼月德江，與陸軍相表裡。

translations.literal: and separately recruited a hundred braves to hold the Nguyet Duc River, coordinating with the land army inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: and separately raised a hundred braves to block the Nguyet Duc River, working in concert with the main army on land and water.

sentences.zh: 」附請吏部主事唐景崧留軍。

translations.literal: " He appended a request that the Ministry of Personnel director Tang Jingsong remain with the army.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked that Ministry of Personnel director Tang Jingsong be kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 初，法人犯順安，越未敗，遽乞和。

translations.literal: At first, when the French attacked Thuan An, Annam had not yet been defeated but hastily sued for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the French attacked Thuan An, Vietnam had not yet been beaten but already rushed to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 延旭奏言：「越人倉卒議和，或謂因故君未葬，冀緩須臾；

translations.literal: Yanxu memorialized saying: "The Annamese are hastily negotiating peace; some say it is because the former ruler is not yet buried and they hope to gain a brief respite;
translations.idiomatic: Yanxu memorialized: "The Vietnamese are hastily negotiating peace. Some say they hope for a brief respite because the former ruler is not yet buried;

sentences.zh: 或謂因廢立嫌疑，朋興黨禍。

translations.literal: others say it is because of suspicions over deposition and enthronement, with factions stirring up party strife.
translations.idiomatic: others attribute it to suspicions surrounding the succession, with factions stirring up partisan strife.

sentences.zh: 越臣黃佐炎等錄寄和約，越誠無以保社稷，中國又何以固籓籬？

translations.literal: The Annamese minister Huang Zuoyan and others copied and sent the peace treaty; if Annam truly cannot preserve its altars of state, how can China secure its frontier barrier?
translations.idiomatic: The Vietnamese minister Huang Zuoyan and others forwarded a copy of the peace treaty. If Vietnam truly cannot preserve its state, how can China secure its frontier bulwark?

sentences.zh: 劉永福現駐山西，法人擬益師往攻，請毋撤兵，用警戎備。

translations.literal: Liu Yongfu is now stationed at Son Tay; the French plan to add troops to attack there—please do not withdraw the army and thereby warn them to tighten military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yongfu is now at Son Tay, and the French intend to reinforce and attack there. I beg that our troops not be withdrawn, so as to keep the border on alert.

sentences.zh: 」越王阮福升嗣位，遣使告哀，並懇允其詣闕乞封；

translations.literal: " The Annamese king Nguyen Phuc Thang succeeded to the throne, sent envoys to announce mourning, and also earnestly requested permission for him to come to court to beg investiture;
translations.idiomatic: " The Vietnamese king Nguyen Phuc Thang had succeeded to the throne and sent envoys to announce mourning, earnestly requesting permission for him to come to court and beg investiture;

sentences.zh: 复具和約二十七條及黃佐炎禀，上之樞府。

translations.literal: he also submitted the twenty-seven articles of the peace treaty together with Huang Zuoyan's report, forwarding them to the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: he also submitted the twenty-seven articles of the peace treaty together with Huang Zuoyan's report to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠檄前布政使王德榜募勇扼桂邊，朝命受延旭節度。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang ordered the former provincial treasurer Wang Debang to recruit braves to block the Guangxi border; the court commanded that he accept Yanxu's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang ordered former provincial treasurer Wang Debang to raise braves to hold the Guangxi border, and the court placed him under Yanxu's command.

sentences.zh: 其冬，力疾再出關，駐諒山，趣軍進取，分襲海陽、嘉林綴敵勢；

translations.literal: That winter, forcing himself though ill he again went out through the pass, halted at Lang Son, urged the army forward to seize ground, and divided attacks on Hai Duong and Gia Lam to pin down the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: That winter, though gravely ill, he again crossed the border and encamped at Lang Son, pressing the army to advance and launching diversionary strikes on Hai Duong and Gia Lam to pin down the enemy;

sentences.zh: 並請撥船嚴扼海口，斷其出入：諭仍力守北寧。

translations.literal: he also requested boats to be assigned to block the sea mouths strictly and cut off their entry and exit: he was instructed still to hold Bac Ninh with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked that vessels be deployed to block the river mouths and cut French access. The court instructed him nonetheless to hold Bac Ninh firmly.

sentences.zh: 於是令左軍黃桂蘭、右軍趙沃協防其地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the left army under Huang Guilan and the right army under Zhao Wo to defend the place jointly.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Huang Guilan's left wing and Zhao Wo's right wing to defend the position jointly.

sentences.zh: 適山西陷，延旭猶慮兵力薄，復遣使入關募勇，通舊五十餘營，厚集於此。

translations.literal: Just then Son Tay fell; Yanxu still worried that his forces were thin and again sent envoys into the pass to recruit braves, mustering more than fifty former battalions in strength at this point.
translations.idiomatic: Son Tay had just fallen, and Yanxu, still fearing his forces were too thin, again sent men back through the pass to recruit braves, assembling more than fifty former battalions on the spot.

sentences.zh: 隨令廣間諜，安地營，禁擾民，嚴冒餉；

translations.literal: He then ordered widespread use of spies, secure encampments, prohibition of harassing the people, and strict punishment of false muster rolls;
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered wider use of spies, secure camps, strict bans on harassing civilians, and harsh penalties for padded payrolls;

sentences.zh: 然沃等皆寡識，桂蘭尤侈汰，與越官張登壇日事宴樂。

translations.literal: yet Wo and the others were all shallow in judgment, while Guilan was especially extravagant and, with the Annamese official Zhang Dengtan, daily gave themselves to feasting and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: yet Zhao Wo and his fellows were all men of little judgment, while Huang Guilan was especially extravagant and spent his days feasting with the Vietnamese official Zhang Dengtan.

sentences.zh: 登壇故通法，嗣以有郤洩其事。

translations.literal: Dengtan had long been in communication with the French; later, because of a grudge, he leaked the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Dengtan had long been in contact with the French; later, after a personal quarrel, he exposed the connection.

sentences.zh: 上命延旭罷登壇，或囚而殺之，延旭以力不能制而止。

translations.literal: The throne ordered Yanxu to dismiss Dengtan or imprison and execute him; Yanxu stopped because he lacked the power to control the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Yanxu to remove Dengtan or imprison and execute him, but Yanxu desisted because he lacked the power to enforce it.

sentences.zh: 日唯籌軍火濟師，以為兵力厚，可恃以無恐。

translations.literal: Day after day he only planned munitions to supply the army, thinking that with thick forces he could rely on them without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he busied himself only with procuring arms and supplies, believing that with so many troops massed he had nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 桂蘭復希風指，侈談部下能戰，延旭益信之，遂六上書請戰。

translations.literal: Guilan again watched the wind of opinion and extravagantly talked of his subordinates' ability to fight; Yanxu trusted him all the more and thus six times memorialized requesting battle.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guilan again read which way the wind blew and boasted extravagantly of his men's fighting power. Yanxu believed him all the more and memorialized six times asking to give battle.

sentences.zh: 上不許，敕保守未失陷地，毋貪功。

translations.literal: The throne did not consent and ordered him to hold conservatively the territory not yet lost and not to be greedy for merit.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused and ordered him to hold whatever ground had not yet fallen and not seek merit rashly.

sentences.zh: 十年，法軍陷扶良，三路攻北寧，桂蘭潰奔太原。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the French army took Phu Luong; on three roads they attacked Bac Ninh, and Guilan broke and fled toward Thai Nguyen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the French took Phu Luong and attacked Bac Ninh on three routes. Huang Guilan's force collapsed and fled toward Thai Nguyen.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章電奏失守，延旭猶上言：「西聯滇軍，東防江口，北寧斷無他虞。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang telegraphed memorializing the loss of the position; Yanxu still reported upward: "Linking with the Yunnan army in the west and blocking the river mouth in the east, Bac Ninh assuredly has no other worry.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang telegraphed reporting the fall of the position, yet Yanxu still wrote: "With the Yunnan army linked on the west and the river mouth blocked on the east, Bac Ninh is surely secure.

sentences.zh: 」上責其飾詞。

translations.literal: " The throne reproached him for glossing over the facts.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne rebuked him for dressing up the truth.

sentences.zh: 會岑毓英抵保勝，部署邊外各軍，遂命延旭軍屬之。

translations.literal: When Cen Yuying reached Bao Sheng and deployed the various armies beyond the border, Yanxu's forces were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Cen Yuying reached Bao Sheng and deployed the frontier armies, Yanxu's troops were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 初，延旭之任西撫也，未及兩月，亦知桂蘭等未可恃。

translations.literal: At first, when Yanxu took up the post of governor of the western provinces, in less than two months he also knew that Guilan and the others could not be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanxu first took up his post as governor of the western provinces, within two months he already knew Huang Guilan and his ilk could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 嗣以臨敵易將，操之急，易生變，以故誥誡備至；

translations.literal: Later, because changing generals on the eve of battle and pressing them too hard easily produced mutiny, for that reason he admonished them in the utmost detail;
translations.idiomatic: Later, fearing that replacing commanders on the eve of battle or pressing them too hard would provoke mutiny, he admonished them at length;

sentences.zh: 而桂蘭等且縱兵剽奪，越民不堪命，忿滋甚。

translations.literal: yet Guilan and the others also let their troops plunder and rob, and the Annamese people could not bear it—their resentment grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: yet Huang Guilan and the others still let their men plunder at will. The Vietnamese populace could not endure it, and their resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 是役也，群反噬，城乃陷。

translations.literal: In this campaign the masses turned and bit back, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle the local people turned on the Chinese troops, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 延旭上其欺飾狀，並自糾請治罪。

translations.literal: Yanxu reported upward on their deceit and concealment and also impeached himself requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxu reported their deception and also impeached himself, asking to be punished.

sentences.zh: 上怒，詔革職留任。

translations.literal: The throne was angry and ordered him dismissed from office but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was furious and stripped him of rank while keeping him at his post.

sentences.zh: 法軍乘勝入芹驛關，復命力扞之，毋再失。

translations.literal: The French army pressed their victory into Qin Yi Pass; he was again ordered to resist it with all his strength and not lose ground again.
translations.idiomatic: The French pressed their victory into Qin Yi Pass, and he was again ordered to hold the line and lose no more ground.

sentences.zh: 延旭以景崧護軍收殘兵，更約束，令駐屯梅。

translations.literal: Yanxu had Jingsong protect the army, gather the broken troops, impose discipline anew, and order them to garrison Tun Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxu put Tang Jingsong in charge of gathering the shattered units, restoring discipline, and garrisoning Tun Mei.

sentences.zh: 時諒江、朗山、狼甲相繼屠潰，諒山教民且蠢焉思動。

translations.literal: At that time Lang Giang, Lang Son, and Lang Giap were slaughtered and routed in succession, and the Lang Son Catholics were also stirring as if to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Giang, Lang Son, and Lang Giap were overrun in turn, and the Catholic communities around Lang Son were also restless and ready to rise.

sentences.zh: 延旭鑑覆轍，嚴禁防軍向越官索夫米，有伐一草一木者斬，越民仍不知感。

translations.literal: Yanxu took warning from the repeated collapse, strictly forbade the defense troops to demand laborers and rice from Annamese officials, and ordered death for anyone who cut a single plant—but the Annamese people still did not feel gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Learning from past disasters, Yanxu strictly forbade his troops to demand corvée and rice from Vietnamese officials and decreed death for anyone who cut so much as a blade of grass, yet the Vietnamese still felt no gratitude.

sentences.zh: 適德榜至，勸延旭勉自支振，圖再舉。

translations.literal: Just then Debang arrived and urged Yanxu to brace himself and strive for a fresh effort.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Debang then arrived and urged Yanxu to rally himself and plan another effort.

sentences.zh: 於是更嚴勒粵軍，仿楚勇制，力求後效。

translations.literal: Thereupon he tightened discipline on the Guangdong troops still further, modeled them on the Hunan braves' system, and strove for results afterward.
translations.idiomatic: He then tightened discipline on the Guangdong troops further, modeled them on the Hunan brave system, and strove for better results.

sentences.zh: 而逮問之命下，吏議斬監候，改戍新疆。

translations.literal: But the order for arrest and interrogation came down; the officials deliberated decapitation followed by imprisonment awaiting execution, commuted to banishment to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: But the order for arrest and trial arrived; the judicial officials recommended decapitation with imprisonment pending execution, commuted to exile in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 追論舉主，之洞、佩綸，均被訶責。

translations.literal: Tracing responsibility to those who had recommended him, Zhidong and Peilun were both severely reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: His sponsors Zhang Zhidong and Zhang Peilun were both severely reprimanded in turn.

sentences.zh: 延旭未出都，病卒。

translations.literal: Before Yanxu left the capital he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxu died of illness before he could leave the capital.

sentences.zh: 子坊，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Fang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 唐炯，字鄂生，貴州遵義人。

translations.literal: Tang Jiong, style name Esheng, was a native of Zunyi in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jiong, whose style was Esheng, came from Zunyi in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年舉人，訓方子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the provincial examination; he was the son of Tang Xunfang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang and was the son of Tang Xunfang.

sentences.zh: 訓方督師金口，炯馳數千里省視。

translations.literal: When Xunfang commanded the army at Jinkou, Jiong raced several thousand li to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunfang was commanding at Jinkou, Jiong traveled thousands of li to visit him.

sentences.zh: 越夕難作，倉皇奉遺疏謁曾國籓，得代奏。

translations.literal: The next evening disaster struck; in haste he carried the final memorial and called on Zeng Guofan, obtaining permission to present it on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster struck the very next night. He hurried off with his father's final memorial to Zeng Guofan and secured permission to present it on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 武昌复，求遺骸歸葬。

translations.literal: When Wuchang was recovered he sought the remains and returned them for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang was recovered he recovered his father's remains and brought them home for burial.

sentences.zh: 桐梓亂民起，治鄉團御之。

translations.literal: When disorderly people rose in Tongzi he organized local militia to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When unrest broke out in Tongzi he organized local militia to resist it.

sentences.zh: 服闋，入貲為知縣，銓四川。

translations.literal: When mourning was over he purchased an office as magistrate and was assigned to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period he bought an office as magistrate and was assigned to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，署南溪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Nanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Nanxi.

sentences.zh: 值滇寇李永和蠢動，藍朝柱應之，陷敘州，吏士皆恐。

translations.literal: Just then the Yunnan bandit Li Yonghe stirred up trouble and Lan Chaozhu responded; they took Xu Prefecture and officials and gentry were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunnan rebel Li Yonghe was then on the move, with Lan Chaozhu joining him; they seized Xu Prefecture and officials and gentry alike were terrified.

sentences.zh: 炯乃訓練兵壯，晨夜徼循，人心稍靖。

translations.literal: Jiong then trained the militia, patrolled day and night, and popular feeling gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong trained the militia, patrolled day and night, and the populace gradually settled.

sentences.zh: 有為寇所獲者，縱之還，曰：「為我語唐青天，決不犯南溪一草一木！

translations.literal: When someone was captured by the bandits they released him and said: "Tell Magistrate Tang the Blue Sky for me—we will certainly not violate a single plant in Nanxi!
translations.idiomatic: When bandits captured one of his men they sent him back with the message: "Tell Magistrate Tang the Blue Sky for us—we will not touch a blade of grass in Nanxi!

sentences.zh: 」炯領兵偪吊黃樓，單騎入營，諭以利害，朝柱款附。

translations.literal: " Jiong led troops to press Diaohuang Tower, entered the camp alone on horseback, and expounded advantage and harm; Chaozhu submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong advanced on Diaohuang Tower, rode alone into the rebel camp, and laid out the stakes; Lan Chaozhu submitted.

sentences.zh: 永和改犯犍為，炯馳救，壁不動，俟其懈乘之，寇狂奔，自相轔藉。

translations.literal: Yonghe then shifted to attack Qianwei; Jiong raced to the rescue, held the walls without moving, and when they slackened struck them; the bandits fled wildly, trampling one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe then turned to attack Qianwei. Jiong rushed to the rescue, held the walls without stirring, and when the enemy relaxed struck; the rebels fled in panic, trampling one another.

sentences.zh: 旋與楚軍解成都圍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he joined the Hunan army in relieving the siege of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the Hunan army in lifting the siege of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 八年，檄署綿州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered by dispatch to act in Mianzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was ordered by dispatch to handle affairs in Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時郫、彭軍事棘，調還省防守。

translations.literal: At that time military affairs in Pi and Peng were critical; he was transferred back to the province for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs in Pi and Peng were then critical, and he was recalled to the provincial capital for defense.

sentences.zh: 炯诇得黑窩盜虛實，請限八日畢乃事，果如所言。

translations.literal: Jiong spied out the real strength of the Heiwodao bandits, asked for a limit of eight days to finish the affair, and it turned out as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong reconnoitered the Heiwodao bandits' true strength, asked for eight days to finish the job, and finished on schedule.

sentences.zh: 除知夔州，未上，踰月，永和圍綿城，炯掘壕登陴，民助貲糧。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Kuizhou but had not taken up the post when, after a month, Yonghe besieged Mian City; Jiong dug moats and mounted the battlements, and the people helped with funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Kuizhou but had not assumed office when, a month later, Yonghe besieged Mian City. Jiong dug trenches and manned the walls, and the people supplied money and grain.

sentences.zh: 炯居城三月，不下，誓死守；

translations.literal: Jiong remained in the city three months without yielding and swore to defend to the death;
translations.idiomatic: Jiong held the city for three months without yielding and swore to die defending it;

sentences.zh: 援至，圍始解。

translations.literal: when relief arrived the siege was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: when relief arrived the siege was at last broken.

sentences.zh: 已而湘、黔軍閧州署，駱秉章劾罷之。

translations.literal: Before long Hunan and Guizhou troops rioted at the prefectural yamen; Luo Bingzhang impeached and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hunan and Guizhou troops rioted at the prefectural yamen; Luo Bingzhang impeached and dismissed the commanders involved.

sentences.zh: 事白，仍治軍。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared he still commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was cleared he resumed military command.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，統安定營。

translations.literal: At the change to the Tongzhi reign he commanded the Anding battalion.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tongzhi he took command of the Anding battalion.

sentences.zh: 會石達開圍涪州，與劉岳昭期會師，擊走之。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai besieged Fuzhou he joined Liu Yuezhao in a scheduled rendezvous and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai besieged Fuzhou he joined Liu Yuezhao as planned and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 其夏，石黨窺綦江。

translations.literal: That summer Shi's followers watched for an opening at Qijiang.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Shi's followers probed Qijiang for an opening.

sentences.zh: 炯聞警馳援，燔其壁，寇潰，大破之長寧。

translations.literal: Jiong heard the alarm and raced to reinforce, burned their stockade, the bandits broke, and he inflicted a great defeat on them at Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Jiong rushed to reinforce, burned their camp, routed them, and won a great victory at Changning.

sentences.zh: 以疾還成都。

translations.literal: Because of illness he returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Illness then forced his return to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 秉章詢寇勢，時寇退滇邊，聲入黔，炯曰：「此誘我軍東下耳。

translations.literal: Bingzhang inquired about the bandit situation; at the time the bandits had retreated to the Yunnan border with noise of entering Guizhou; Jiong said: "This is to lure our army eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang asked about the rebels' movements. They had retreated toward the Yunnan border while rumors spread of a thrust into Guizhou. Jiong said: "This is a feint to draw our army east.

sentences.zh: 彼必走夷地，乘虛入川，寧越宜警備。

translations.literal: They are sure to run into the Yi lands and, seizing an opening, enter Sichuan; Ningyue and Yibin should be on alert.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely slip into the Yi country and, finding an opening, invade Sichuan. Ningyue and Yibin should stay on guard.

sentences.zh: 」俄而寇入紫地，复請遣唐友耕軍大渡河扼之。

translations.literal: " Before long the bandits entered Zidi; he again requested that Tang Yougeng's army be sent to hold the line at the Dadu River.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the rebels entered Zidi, and he again asked that Tang Yougeng's force be sent to block the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 達開返西岸，退為倮夷所窘，食盡乞降，梟誅之。

translations.literal: Dakai returned to the west bank, retreated and was pressed by the Lolo Yi, food ran out and he begged to surrender, and he was executed by decapitation and display.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai recrossed to the west bank, was harried by the Lolo Yi, ran out of food, and surrendered. He was beheaded and his head displayed.

sentences.zh: 明年，權綏定府，區邑為八路，路若干場，場若干寨，置寨總，行記善惡法，月朔上其簿親判之；

translations.literal: The next year he held acting authority over Suining prefecture, divided the districts into eight routes, with so many markets per route and so many stockades per market, established stockade chiefs, enforced a register of good and evil, and on the first of each month they submitted their registers for his personal judgment;
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as acting prefect of Suining, divided the territory into eight routes with markets and stockades under each, appointed stockade chiefs, enforced a register of good and evil deeds, and on the first of each month had them submit their registers for his personal review;

sentences.zh: 又立書院二、社學八十餘：境內稱治，下其法他縣。

translations.literal: he also established two academies and more than eighty village schools: within the territory it was called well governed, and his methods were applied in other counties.
translations.idiomatic: he also founded two academies and more than eighty village schools. The region was said to be well governed, and other counties adopted his methods.

sentences.zh: 越二年，赴陝佐治營田。

translations.literal: Two years later he went to Shaanxi to assist in managing military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he went to Shaanxi to help administer military colonies.

sentences.zh: 捻首張總愚犯新豐，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Nian leader Zhang Zongyu attacked Xinfeng and was badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian leader Zhang Zongyu attacked Xinfeng and was badly defeated.

sentences.zh: 六年，四川總督崇實命率師入黔。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Sichuan Governor Chong Shi ordered him to lead troops into Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Sichuan Governor Chong Shi ordered him to lead troops into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 黔患貧瘠，崇實先問以理財策，炯曰：「理財莫若節用，節用莫若裁勇，裁勇莫若援黔。

translations.literal: Guizhou suffered from poverty and barrenness; Chong Shi first asked him for a policy on managing finances; Jiong said: "To manage finances nothing surpasses economizing expenditure; to economize expenditure nothing surpasses cutting braves; to cut braves nothing surpasses aiding Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou was poor and exhausted. Chong Shi first asked his views on finance. Jiong said: "Sound finance begins with cutting expenses; cutting expenses begins with reducing irregular troops; reducing irregular troops begins with pacifying Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 」崇實然其言，遂以軍事屬之。

translations.literal: " Chong Shi approved his words and thereupon placed military affairs in his hands.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong Shi approved and placed military affairs in his hands.

sentences.zh: 連破偏刀、水上、大平、黃飄、白堡，擒斬王超凡、劉儀順，降潘人傑、唐天佑，皆積寇也；

translations.literal: In succession he broke Pian Dao, Shuishang, Daping, Huang Piao, and Bai Bao, captured and executed Wang Chaofan and Liu Yishun, and received the surrender of Pan Renjie and Tang Tianyou—all longstanding bandits;
translations.idiomatic: He took Pian Dao, Shuishang, Daping, Huang Piao, and Bai Bao in succession, captured and executed Wang Chaofan and Liu Yishun, and accepted the surrender of Pan Renjie and Tang Tianyou—all long-established bandit chiefs;

sentences.zh: 又克平越、甕安、黃平、清平、麻哈：遷道員，賜號法克精阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: he also took Pingyue, Weng'an, Huangping, Qingping, and Ma Ha: he was promoted to circuit intendant and granted the title Fakexing A Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: he also recovered Pingyue, Weng'an, Huangping, Qingping, and Ma Ha, was promoted to circuit intendant, and was granted the title Fakexing A Batulu.

sentences.zh: 嗣為吳棠所劾，還蜀。

translations.literal: Later he was impeached by Wu Tang and returned to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Tang impeached him and he returned to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，丁寶楨督四川，令佐治鹽筴，旋補建昌道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu Ding Baozhen governed Sichuan and ordered him to assist in managing the salt administration; soon he was appointed Jianchang circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu, when Ding Baozhen became governor of Sichuan, he put Jiong in charge of salt affairs and soon appointed him Jianchang circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 六年，署鹽茶道，條上善後六事，謂：「發引必先新後舊；

translations.literal: In the sixth year he acted as salt and tea circuit intendant and submitted six items for sound administration afterward, stating: "Issuing salt certificates must put new before old;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as acting salt and tea intendant and submitted six reforms, stating: "Salt certificates must be issued new before old;

sentences.zh: 徵稅必先課後引；

translations.literal: collecting tax must put assessment after certificate;
translations.idiomatic: tax must be collected only after the certificate is assessed;

sentences.zh: 收發鹽引，責成鹽道；

translations.literal: issuing and receiving salt certificates shall be the responsibility of the salt intendant;
translations.idiomatic: issuing and receiving salt certificates shall be the salt intendant's responsibility;

sentences.zh: 改代引張，責成州縣；

translations.literal: changing proxy certificate agents shall be the responsibility of prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: replacing proxy certificate agents shall fall to the prefectures and counties;

sentences.zh: 繳殘則嚴定限期；

translations.literal: surrendering leftover certificates shall have strict fixed deadlines;
translations.idiomatic: surrender of leftover certificates shall follow strict deadlines;

sentences.zh: 辦公則優給公費。

translations.literal: for official business generous public funds shall be provided.
translations.idiomatic: official business shall receive adequate public funds.

sentences.zh: 」議行，凡百餘年引目渾殽、款項轇轕諸弊，至是盡革，語具鹽法志。

translations.literal: " The proposals were adopted; abuses of more than a hundred years such as confused certificate registers and tangled accounts were at this point entirely reformed—the details are in the Salt Law Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: " The reforms were adopted. Abuses of more than a century—confused certificate registers, tangled accounts, and the like—were swept away; the details appear in the Salt Law Treatise.

sentences.zh: 八年，張之洞、張佩綸先後奏薦堪軍事，於是擢雲南布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Zhang Zhidong and Zhang Peilun successively memorialized recommending him as capable in military affairs, and he was thereupon promoted to Yunnan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Zhang Zhidong and Zhang Peilun again recommended him for military service, and he was promoted to Yunnan provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 炯率川軍千人駐關外，滇軍悉歸節度。

translations.literal: Jiong led a thousand Sichuan troops to garrison beyond the pass, and all Yunnan forces were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong led a thousand Sichuan troops to camp beyond the border, and all Yunnan forces were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，裁夫馬，治廠務，並釐卡，清田糧，民困少蘇。

translations.literal: Once he took up affairs he cut porter and horse levies, managed factory affairs, consolidated transit duties, and cleared land tax registers; the people's hardships were somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he cut porter and horse levies, reorganized government workshops, consolidated transit duties, and cleared land-tax registers, easing the people's burdens somewhat.

sentences.zh: 法人奪我越南，被命赴開化防守，即於軍前除巡撫。

translations.literal: The French seized our Vietnam; he was ordered to go to Kaihua to defend and was appointed governor on the spot before the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the French seized Vietnam, he was ordered to Kaihua on defensive duty and appointed governor in the field.

sentences.zh: 誤聞將議和，亟還省履任。

translations.literal: Mistakenly hearing that peace was about to be negotiated, he hastened back to the province to assume his post.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing wrongly that peace talks were imminent, he hurried back to the provincial capital to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，褫職逮問，刑部定讞斬監候。

translations.literal: The throne was greatly angered, stripped him of office and ordered arrest and trial; the Ministry of Justice fixed the sentence as decapitation with imprisonment awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was furious, stripped him of rank, and ordered arrest and trial. The Ministry of Justice sentenced him to decapitation with imprisonment pending execution.

sentences.zh: 久之，上意解，三歷秋審，赦歸。

translations.literal: After a long time the throne's anger eased; through three autumn reviews he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor relented. After three autumn reviews he was pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠臚其治行上於朝，命戍雲南，交岑毓英差序。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang set forth his record of good administration to the court and ordered him exiled to Yunnan under Cen Yuying's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang memorialized his administrative record, and the court ordered him to serve in Yunnan under Cen Yuying's direction.

sentences.zh: 十三年，賞巡撫銜，督辦雲南礦務，偕日本礦師躬履昭通、東川、威寧銅鉛各廠，疏陳變通章程，又歷請減免貴州鉛課，豁免雲南礦廠官欠民欠，並報可。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was granted the title of acting governor and supervised Yunnan mining affairs; together with Japanese mining engineers he personally visited the copper and lead works at Zhaotong, Dongchuan, and Weining, memorialized revised regulations, and repeatedly requested reduction of Guizhou lead levies and exemption of official and private arrears at Yunnan mines—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was granted acting governor rank and put in charge of Yunnan mining. With Japanese mining engineers he personally inspected the copper and lead works at Zhaotong, Dongchuan, and Weining, submitted revised regulations, and repeatedly sought reductions in Guizhou lead levies and forgiveness of official and private mine debts in Yunnan—all approved.

sentences.zh: 惟經營十五年，僅歲解京銅百萬斤，為時論所譏。

translations.literal: Yet though he managed affairs for fifteen years he supplied only a million jin of copper to the capital annually and was ridiculed by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after fifteen years of management he delivered only a million jin of copper to the capital each year, drawing ridicule from contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，謝病歸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he resigned for illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，以鄉舉重逢，晉太子少保。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, meeting the juren reunion celebration, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, on the juren reunion celebration, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 逾歲卒，年八十，卹如製。

translations.literal: A year later he died at the age of eighty; mourning rites followed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at eighty; mourning rites followed regulations.

sentences.zh: 何璟，字小宋，廣東香山人。

translations.literal: He Jing, style name Xiaosong, was a native of Xiangshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He Jing, whose style was Xiaosong, came from Xiangshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 父曰愈，見循吏傳。

translations.literal: His father Yi is treated in the Biographies of Conscientious Officials.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi has a biography among the Conscientious Officials.

sentences.zh: 璟，道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，轉御史。

translations.literal: Jing passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler, then transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jing received his jinshi in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed compiler, and later became a censor.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，英人陷廣州，總督葉名琛獲譴罷，而巡撫柏貴等罪相埒，譴弗及，時論譁然，璟乃分別上其謬誤狀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng, when the English took Guangzhou, Governor Ye Mingchen was punished and dismissed while Governor Bok Kui and others were guilty to the same degree yet escaped censure—public opinion was in an uproar—and Jing then separately reported upward on their errors.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng, when the British took Guangzhou, Governor Ye Mingchen was punished and dismissed, yet Governor Bok Kui and others were equally culpable yet escaped blame, provoking public outrage. Jing then submitted separate memorials detailing their errors.

sentences.zh: 明年，英艦入津沽，疏陳戰守要略，先後抗論外務，疏凡八上。

translations.literal: The next year, when English ships entered the Taku mouths, he memorialized essentials of war and defense and in succession argued against foreign affairs in eight memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when British ships entered the Taku mouths, he memorialized on essentials of war and defense and submitted eight successive memorials on foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為安徽廬鳳道。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out as Anhui Lu-Feng circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was sent out as Anhui Lu-Feng circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 捻至，與總兵喻吉三隨方應禦，寇不得逞。

translations.literal: When the Nian arrived he joined Regional Commander Yu Jisan in responding wherever needed, and the bandits could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian rebels appeared he joined Regional Commander Yu Jisan in meeting them wherever they struck, and the rebels could not gain the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 四年，晉湖北布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Hubei provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Hubei provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，到官，值黃陂飢嗛，民就食江、漢，便宜發帑金濟之。

translations.literal: A year later, when he reached his post, Huangpi was suffering famine; the people went to the Yangtze and Han for food, and he expediently disbursed treasury funds to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: A year after taking office, Huangpi was stricken by famine and people went to the Yangtze and Han for food; he promptly disbursed treasury funds for relief.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢福建巡撫，歷山西、江蘇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Fujian governor and served in turn in Shanxi and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Fujian governor and later served in Shanxi and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，服闋，起閩浙總督。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed Min-Zhe governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，備日本議起，治海防，飭戎政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu, as Japanese negotiations arose, he managed coastal defense and tightened military administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu, as negotiations with Japan arose, he managed coastal defense and tightened military discipline.

sentences.zh: 其夏患水祲，日坐城上督拯難民，凡閱七晝夜，醵金卹之。

translations.literal: That summer, when flood disaster struck, he sat daily on the city wall supervising relief for refugees, for seven days and nights in all, and raised funds to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: That summer floods struck. For seven days and nights he sat on the city wall directing relief for refugees and raised funds for their support.

sentences.zh: 水退，濬洪塘江，導支流入海，後患稍殺。

translations.literal: When the waters receded he dredged the Hongtang River and led branch streams into the sea; the disaster afterward was somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When the waters receded he dredged the Hongtang River and channeled branch streams to the sea, and later flooding was somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he also acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he also served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 時日本議廢琉球，數以兵艦浮閩、滬。

translations.literal: At that time Japan was negotiating abolition of the Ryukyu kingdom and repeatedly sent warships to float off Fujian and Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Japan was negotiating the abolition of the Ryukyu kingdom and repeatedly sent warships off Fujian and Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 璟以台灣地當要衝，基隆尤扼全台形勝，乃調集輪舶，增募兵勇，建築砲台，備不虞。

translations.literal: Jing held that Taiwan's territory was strategically critical and Keelung especially commanded the whole island's terrain; he therefore assembled steam vessels, increased recruitment of troops, built batteries, and prepared against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Jing held that Taiwan was strategically vital and Keelung especially commanded the island's terrain. He assembled steam vessels, increased troop recruitment, built batteries, and prepared for contingencies.

sentences.zh: 九年，法越事起，海防戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the French-Vietnamese affair arose, coastal defense was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the French-Vietnamese conflict arose, coastal defenses were placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 璟令總兵張得勝等分扼諸郡，提督孫開華等分扼台、澎，並檄楊在元署台灣鎮，助防守。

translations.literal: Jing ordered Regional Commander Zhang Desheng and others to hold the various prefectures separately and Naval Commander Sun Kaihua and others to hold Taiwan and Penghu separately, and also ordered Yang Zaiyuan to act as Taiwan military commander to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jing ordered Regional Commander Zhang Desheng and others to hold the various prefectures and Naval Commander Sun Kaihua and others to hold Taiwan and Penghu, and also appointed Yang Zaiyuan acting Taiwan military commander to assist in defense.

sentences.zh: 明年，又上福、廈、台益船募卒狀，上皆勗勵之。

translations.literal: The next year he again memorialized on increasing ships and recruiting troops for Fuzhou, Xiamen, and Taiwan; the throne encouraged him in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized again on increasing ships and recruiting troops for Fuzhou, Xiamen, and Taiwan, and the throne encouraged him in each case.

sentences.zh: 已而會辦軍務，張佩綸至，事皆專決，視璟等若屬吏；

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned to manage military affairs; when Zhang Peilun arrived, all affairs were decided solely by him, treating Jing and the others as subordinate officials;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to manage military affairs. When Zhang Peilun arrived, Peilun decided everything alone and treated Jing and the others as subordinates;

sentences.zh: 又嚴劾在元貪謬，璟坐疏忽，幹吏議。

translations.literal: he also sternly impeached Zaiyuan for corruption and incompetence; Jing was punished for negligence and implicated in the officials' deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun also impeached Zaiyuan for corruption and incompetence, and Jing was punished for negligence in the judicial review.

sentences.zh: 以是益畏事之，不敢為異同。

translations.literal: For this reason he feared affairs all the more and did not dare to differ.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he feared taking initiative and dared not dissent.

sentences.zh: 佩綸調舟師砲船局，璟亦以砲布衙署自衛。

translations.literal: Peilun transferred the gunboat bureau's vessels; Jing also placed cannon around the governor's yamen for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun took over the gunboat bureau's fleet; Jing also placed cannon around the governor's yamen for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 廷旨以閩事亟，諄諄諭固守。

translations.literal: Court orders said Fujian affairs were urgent and repeatedly instructed firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Court orders stressed the urgency of Fujian affairs and repeatedly instructed firm defense.

sentences.zh: 逮戰書至，璟告佩綸曰：「明日法人將乘潮攻馬尾矣！

translations.literal: When the declaration of war arrived Jing told Peilun: "Tomorrow the French will attack Mawei on the tide!
translations.idiomatic: When war was declared Jing told Peilun: "Tomorrow the French will attack Mawei on the tide!

sentences.zh: 」佩綸弗聽。

translations.literal: Peilun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 舟師大挫，璟欲馳援，而臨浦無舟可濟，株守省城，卒致閩事日壞；

translations.literal: The naval force suffered a great setback; Jing wished to rush to reinforce but there were no boats at the nearby ford to cross, and he remained stockaded in the provincial capital, so that Fujian affairs grew worse day by day;
translations.idiomatic: The fleet suffered a crushing defeat. Jing wished to rush to reinforce but found no boats at the nearby crossing and remained in the provincial capital, so Fujian affairs deteriorated daily;

sentences.zh: 然猶左袒廣勇，雖逃不問，頗為時訾議。

translations.literal: yet he still favored the Guangdong braves and, though they fled, did not inquire into it—he was much criticized in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: yet he still favored the Guangdong braves and did not punish deserters, drawing much contemporary criticism.

sentences.zh: 乃飛章自劾，而廷旨已先召還京。

translations.literal: He then flew a memorial impeaching himself, but the court order summoning him back to the capital had already come down.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried a memorial impeaching himself, but the court had already ordered his recall to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋御史亦劾其闒冗，部議褫職。

translations.literal: Soon censors also impeached him for slackness and incompetence; the ministry deliberated stripping him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon censors impeached him for slackness and incompetence, and the ministry recommended stripping him of office.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 張兆棟，字友山，山東濰縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhaodong, style name Youshan, was a native of Weixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaodong, whose style was Youshan, came from Weixian in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，銓刑部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned to the Ministry of Justice as a director, and was repeatedly promoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, was assigned to the Ministry of Justice as a director, and rose to department director.

sentences.zh: 出知陝西鳳翔府，蒞事三月，而回寇竊發，乃募鄉兵捍之。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Fengxiang prefecture in Shaanxi; three months after taking office the Hui rebels broke out in secret and he recruited local militia to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Fengxiang in Shaanxi. Three months after taking office the Hui rebels rose, and he recruited local militia to resist.

sentences.zh: 無何，城被圍，寇且掘長壕圖久困，兆棟晨夕登陴慰勞守者。

translations.literal: Before long the city was besieged; the rebels also dug a long moat intending prolonged encirclement; Zhaodong morning and evening mounted the battlements to comfort the defenders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city was besieged. The rebels dug a long trench intending a prolonged siege, and Zhaodong mounted the walls morning and evening to encourage the defenders.

sentences.zh: 寇轟潰西南城，蟻附上，兆棟躬冒矢石，戰甚力，寇不得逞。

translations.literal: The rebels blasted a breach in the southwest wall and swarmed up like ants; Zhaodong personally braved arrows and stones and fought fiercely; the rebels could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels blasted the southwest wall and swarmed up like ants. Zhaodong personally braved arrows and stones and fought fiercely, and the rebels could not break through.

sentences.zh: 益固結紳民，誓堅守，閱十有六月，援師至，圍始解。

translations.literal: He further solidified ties with gentry and people, swore firm defense, and after sixteen months relief arrived and the siege was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the local gentry and people to stand firm. After sixteen months relief arrived and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 超授四川按察使。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Sichuan provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to Sichuan provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，調廣東，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Guangdong and promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Guangdong and promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠治軍嘉應​​，餽運阻絕，兆棟殫心籌畫，給食不乏。

translations.literal: When Zuo Zongtang commanded troops at Jiaying, supply routes were cut off; Zhaodong exhausted himself in planning and provisions did not run short.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo Zongtang commanded troops at Jiaying, supply routes were cut off. Zhaodong threw himself into planning and provisions never ran short.

sentences.zh: 歷安徽、江蘇，皆稱職。

translations.literal: He served in Anhui and Jiangsu and in each place was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Anhui and Jiangsu and in each was considered competent.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Director-General of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 時運河久廢不緝，兆棟慮海警阻漕，為上治河濟運狀，稱旨。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Canal had long fallen into disrepair; Zhaodong feared sea alarms would block grain transport and submitted a memorial to the throne on governing the river and aiding transport that won approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal had long fallen into disrepair. Fearing that maritime alarms would block grain transport, Zhaodong memorialized on river works and transport relief, which the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 十一年，再調廣東。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred again to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred again to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 粵俗嗜博，闈姓害尤烈，疏請禁止，報可，而總督英翰曲徇商人請，弛其禁，兆棟劾之，落職，遂兼攝總督事，禁益嚴，終其任，粵吏無敢言闈姓者。

translations.literal: Cantonese custom was addicted to gambling; the lottery harm was especially severe; he memorialized requesting prohibition and received approval, but Governor Ying Han bent to merchants' requests and relaxed the ban; Zhaodong impeached him, was dismissed from office, and then also acted as governor; the prohibition grew stricter, and throughout his tenure Guangdong officials did not dare speak of the lottery.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese were addicted to gambling, and the lottery was especially harmful. He memorialized to ban it and received approval, but Governor Ying Han yielded to merchants and relaxed the ban. Zhaodong impeached him, was himself dismissed, then also acted as governor, enforced the ban more strictly, and throughout his term no Guangdong official dared mention the lottery.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he returned home on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he returned home for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起福建巡撫。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Fujian governor.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Fujian governor.

sentences.zh: 十年，法越事起，法艦窺台、閩。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the French-Vietnamese affair arose, French ships watched Taiwan and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the French-Vietnamese conflict arose, French ships prowled off Taiwan and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 張佩綸銜命會辦閩防軍務，兆棟畏其焰，曲意事之，日謁如衙參。

translations.literal: Zhang Peilun was ordered to manage Fujian coastal defense; Zhaodong feared his influence and curried favor, visiting him daily as if attending at the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Peilun was ordered to manage Fujian coastal defense. Zhaodong feared his power and curried favor, visiting daily as if reporting to a superior.

sentences.zh: 佩綸虛飾胜狀，詔發萬金犒兆棟軍。

translations.literal: Peilun falsely reported victories; the throne issued ten thousand taels to reward Zhaodong's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun falsely reported victories, and the throne issued ten thousand taels to reward Zhaodong's troops.

sentences.zh: 兆棟且疏劾大員謀遁，意指何璟也，朝旨令據實以聞。

translations.literal: Zhaodong also memorialized impeaching a high official for plotting flight, intending He Jing; the court ordered him to report according to facts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodong also memorialized impeaching a high official for plotting to flee, clearly meaning He Jing; the court ordered him to report according to facts.

sentences.zh: 已而事亟，己亦微服匿民間，數日略定，復出任事。

translations.literal: Before long affairs grew urgent; he himself also went in disguise and hid among the people; after several days things were slightly settled and he again came out to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon affairs grew desperate. He himself went in disguise and hid among the people. After several days matters calmed slightly and he resumed office.

sentences.zh: 璟罷，兆棟兼總督，朝廷論馬尾失守罪，褫職。

translations.literal: When Jing was dismissed Zhaodong also acted as governor; the court judged responsibility for the Mawei defeat and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was dismissed Zhaodong also acted as governor. The court judged responsibility for the Mawei defeat and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒於閩。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，复官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong his office was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong his office was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 論曰：法越初構釁，號識時務者爭上書忼慨言戰。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the French-Vietnamese trouble first arose, those who styled themselves men of insight vied to memorialize boldly in favor of war.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: When the French-Vietnamese conflict first arose, those who styled themselves men of insight competed to memorialize boldly for war.

sentences.zh: 未及旬日，延旭敗退廣西，炯棄關外新安行營。

translations.literal: In less than ten days Yanxu was defeated and retreated to Guangxi, and Jiong abandoned the field camp beyond the pass at Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Yanxu was defeated and retreated to Guangxi, and Jiong abandoned his field camp beyond the pass at Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 何璟、兆棟懾張佩綸之氣勢，怯懦而無所主，事急皆遁。

translations.literal: He Jing and Zhaodong were overawed by Zhang Peilun's influence, were timid and without initiative, and when trouble came all fled.
translations.idiomatic: He Jing and Zhaodong were cowed by Zhang Peilun's prestige, timid and without initiative; when crisis came they all fled.

sentences.zh: 方其互相汲引，不恤舉疆事以輕試；

translations.literal: When they had recommended one another they did not hesitate to stake frontier affairs on a light trial;
translations.idiomatic: When recommending one another they had not hesitated to stake frontier affairs on a rash trial;

sentences.zh: 及其敗也，其黨益肆言熒聽，而此數人者，遂得保首領以沒。

translations.literal: when they were defeated their faction only spread misleading talk all the more, while these several men were able to preserve their heads and die in bed.
translations.idiomatic: when defeated, their faction only spread more misleading talk, yet these men were able to keep their heads and die in bed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷固寬大，亦失刑甚矣。

translations.literal: The court was indeed lenient, but it also failed in punishment too greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The court was indeed lenient—but it also failed greatly in punishment.
